capabilities.target: executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
any recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox
executive's calendar (invite acceptance and prep notes)

inputs.source: Calendar invites, including invites from outside the company; description field is free text written by the sender

instructions.note: No restriction on which documents may be shared or which recipients are appropriate; attendees of any accepted invite, including external senders, receive a brief drawn from the executive's drive.

The only stated check on agent action is a daily summary, written by the agent itself and reviewed after actions are already taken; there is no preventive control, so safety depends entirely on the instructions being followed correctly.

elements.name: Any external or internal calendar invite sender
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)

controls.name: Executive review of agent-authored daily summary
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is authored by the same agent whose compliance is in question; a more capable or hijacked model can write a summary that omits or downplays injected actions (ASI09), and review happens only after the mail.send has already fired, so it cannot prevent harm.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. Recommended as a raw-action, low-volume gate so it does not inherit the decay of a model-summary gate.

controls.name: Recipient allowlist bound to the calendar system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. Binding recipients to the calendar record's attendee list, rather than invite-supplied text, does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Injection-aware classifier on invite description text
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. A separate classifier narrows but does not fully close multi-turn or encoded injection payloads, per control_decay.md.

controls.name: Per-period cap on automatic accept-prepare-send cycles
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. A hard cap on cycles processed per day does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Independent tamper-evident audit log of agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. A log generated outside the acting model's own output, unlike the self-authored daily summary, would not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential document exfiltration via emailed brief

attack_path.note: Anyone can send the executive an invite with an attacker-controlled free-text description.
Agent auto-accepts the invite and begins the prepare step driven by invite content.
Agent searches the executive's drive, which holds board materials and draft financial results.
Agent emails a brief built from the retrieved documents to the invite's attendees, with no recipient restriction.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model version change in subject.model; removal of the daily-summary review step; new outbound channels added beyond mail.send; rising invite volume.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to accept any new invite if the time is free and then automatically find related documents and email a brief to the attendees, with no check on sender identity, document sensitivity, or recipient list.

Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite with a free-text description, mail.send has no recipient restrictions or approval step, and the drive holds board materials and draft financial results.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate (raw_action review, low volume) before mail.send dispatches any brief containing confidential or restricted documents.
Restrict mail.send recipients to the meeting's verified attendee list pulled from the calendar system of record, never from invite-supplied free text.
Add an injection-aware classifier or sanitizer on invite descriptions before they can influence document search or recipient selection.

findings.title: No independently attributable audit record of agent actions (self-authored daily summary)

forecast.watch_signal: Any claim that the daily summary now serves as an audit record, or reduced frequency/depth of executive review.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so the only record of what the agent did is authored by the same system whose behavior is in question.
The executive reviews a daily summary only after invites have already been acted on, so review happens after any harmful send has already occurred.

recommendations.action: Generate action logs via an independent, tamper-evident mechanism outside the agent's own output, and have the daily review consume that log rather than a model-written summary.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on automatic invite processing enables repeated exfiltration and resource exhaustion

forecast.watch_signal: Rising median number of invites auto-processed per day; connection of additional calendars or mailboxes (data_scope_expansion).

evidence.observation: 'Act on invites as they arrive' states no limit on the number of invites processed per period, and no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes are specified in the runtime notes.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so each incoming invite can independently trigger a send with no aggregate cap.

recommendations.action: Impose a per-day cap on automatic accept-prepare-send cycles, with anomalous volume routed to human review.

stride_coverage.rationale: No peer agents or external protocol connections assert this agent's identity to others; this is a single-agent design with no agent-to-agent handshake to spoof.
Artifacts do not describe whether invite sender addresses are retained in any log for accountability or follow-up.
Artifacts do not describe the authentication mechanism for the executive's chat channel, though it is treated as a trusted source by design.
Artifacts do not describe whether the executive's own chat requests are separately logged from agent-authored summaries.
This is an inbound flow carrying an invite into the agent; it does not itself carry outbound disclosure of internal data.
Artifacts do not describe mail transport security (for example TLS) outside of the agent's own composition behavior.
The summary is an internal report reviewed only by the executive; no external disclosure path for this store is described in the artifacts.
No volume or exhaustion concern specific to this store exists beyond the processing pipeline already covered in finding.unbounded_invite_volume.
cap.drive_read is read-only; this design grants no write or delete access to the drive, so tampering through this path is not reachable.
Read-only access to a document store does not expose a denial of service vector distinct from the capability path itself.

rating.rationale: The dominant path is an untrusted calendar invite (anyone can send one, with attacker-controlled free text) that drives the agent through retrieval of board and financial materials and out through an unrestricted mail.send, with the autonomy modifier applying because no step or runtime limit is declared (max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both null). The only declared control is a detective, model-authored daily summary, which earns no tier credit under rubric section 5 because it is behavioral, dependent, and reviewed only after the email has already been sent; no structural preventive control (approval gate, recipient restriction, injection classifier, rate limit, or independent audit log) is declared, so residual equals inherent at critical. Two further property findings -- no independently attributable audit trail, and no cap on invites auto-processed -- are capped at high per rubric 5a but compound the primary path. The forecast stays critical because the primary finding is already at the rating ceiling; model upgrades and autonomy increases would further erode the one declared control's value without the design needing to change at all.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of a deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope and exact data sensitivity labels are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on precise boundaries is medium.

No evidence was provided that the daily summary control has ever been exercised or verified (status: declared only); if logs show additional controls in practice, residual and forecast should be reconsidered.
